statusText: Tail risk low as NQ futures grind higher inside a narrow 0.43% overnight band; mapped policy state EA_ON with elevated Stress.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail remains in the low band because the overnight advance is a shallow 133.75-point drift that partially retraces the prior session's 1.39% decline, price sits 20-37 points below the band high rather than holding an extreme, and VIX closed 15.41 after fading a 16.46 intraday peak. Elevated Stress reflects long-end yields near 24-year highs after a weak 30-year auction, crude above 90 dollars, the unresolved AI revenue repricing and a second straight weekly decline in Asia. The narrow checkpoint is 13:30-15:00 UTC, covering the cash open and the Michigan preliminary release.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures grind higher in a narrow band as Asia slips and crude eases
body: December NQ futures trade 31,050.25 on Yahoo Finance and 31,067.00 on Investing.com, up 0.26% and 0.31% from a 30,969.50 prior close, inside an overnight band of 30,953.00-31,086.75. That band is only 133.75 points, roughly 0.43%, and price holds its upper half while sitting 20-37 points below the high, so no session-extreme holding and no failed-retracement sequence is observed. The advance partially retraces the prior session rather than extending it: the Nasdaq-100 cash index closed 30,725.81, down 1.39%, after a 30,556.40-31,125.13 range, the Nasdaq Composite fell 1.25% in its worst day since mid-August, and the S&P 500 closed 7,765.36, down about 0.5%. VIX settled 15.41, up 2.19%, after fading an intraday 16.46 high, a low absolute level for a 1.39% index decline that indicates volatility decay rather than expansion. The driver of the decline was a Financial Times report that OpenAI's annualised revenue is near 50 billion dollars rather than the roughly 70 billion investors had inferred, a 20 billion dollar shortfall that cut the Philadelphia semiconductor index 3.4%, with Oracle down 5.5%, Intel 5.3% and Nvidia 2.9%. The bond backdrop is the main unresolved amplifier: the 10-year holds near 5.22-5.23%, close to Wednesday's 24-year high, the 30-year is near 5.60%, and Thursday's 30-year auction cleared 5.618%, some 31 basis points above September's 5.308% and judged weaker than the preceding 10-year sale; the latest H.15 release shows the 2-year at 4.77%. Crude has eased overnight to about 90.88 WTI and 103.44 Brent, down 0.66% and 0.80%, after jumping more than 4% on Hurricane Isaias and the unresolved Hormuz standoff, so the supply premium is decaying rather than building. Isaias is a Category 2 storm with winds near 100 mph, forecast ashore on the northern Gulf Coast between roughly 00:00 and 05:00 UTC Saturday with storm surge of 4 to 8 feet. On the Hormuz file there has been no new escalation: the United States rejected Iran's seven-day reopening proposal in late September and Iran says it awaits a definitive response. In Asia, the Nikkei trades 68,482.63, down 0.81% after trading below 68,330 earlier, with SoftBank near minus 7% and Kioxia near minus 4%, while the Asia-Pacific index excluding Japan is down only 0.16% and heads for a second straight weekly decline; Korea and Taiwan are closed for a holiday. That Asia-versus-NQ divergence reduces directional conviction rather than establishing a one-way path. Tail therefore stays in the low band while the breadth of unresolved catalysts keeps Stress elevated. The shared Finviz context file was dated 29 September, roughly nine days old and marked partial, so it was treated as stale and not used; this assessment rests on independently verified primary sources.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry published Claude assessments. Tail held 10-14 through the Asia and early European hours of 8 October with Stress in the high 40s to mid 50s, stepped into the watch band at the 07:00 UTC handover and ran 20-23 through the European and early US session as the AI-led decline developed. The 17:00 UTC hour was the single elevated reading at Tail 28 with Stress 72 while the semiconductor drop was steepest. Tail then decayed to 16-18 from 20:00 UTC as the cash session recovered off its low and volatility failed to expand, with Confidence steady at 85-89 throughout.
outlookSummary: Tail stays in the low band through the thin Asian hours, easing to 16 as the shallow overnight drift partially retraces the prior decline, then rises gradually to the top of the low band into the 07:00 UTC European handover. It enters the watch band from 09:00 UTC on conditional range-expansion risk and peaks at 22 in the 14:00 UTC hour, which carries the Michigan preliminary release 30 minutes after the 13:30 UTC cash open. That 13:30-15:00 UTC window is the narrow checkpoint. Tail then eases through the US afternoon on a base case of volatility decay, returns to the watch band for the Friday power hour and the 20:00 UTC cash close with a scheduled Fed Collins speech, and falls to 13-14 once index futures reach their 21:00 UTC weekly halt, where no intraday path can form. Confidence declines from 88 to 80 across the horizon purely as a function of distance from the current observation set. Every forecast hour beyond the current one frames price-path structure conditionally.
